findings.reason: At apply.js:52-63 the first marker follows a `-` line, so addEOFNL is set and the `break` skips the second marker, which used to set removeEOFNL. Lines 70-72 then push '' when the source has no trailing newline, so 'old' patched by ['-old','\…','+new','\…'] returns 'new\n' rather than 'new'. createPatch produces exactly this shape (test/patch/create.js:93-107), so the output is silently wrong. Kept at high, not critical: the trigger is traced, but the damage is one wrong trailing newline.
findings.claim: The new `break` stops the EOF-marker scan at the first `\ No newline at end of file`. When the last line changes and neither version ends in a newline, applyPatch now adds a trailing newline that should not be there.
findings.evidence:
The library's own createPatch emits this patch shape: test/patch/create.js:93-107 expects `-line4` / `\ No newline at end of file` / `+line44` / `\ No newline at end of file`. Under fuzzFactor 0, the loop at apply.js:52-63 now sees only the first marker, which follows a `-` line. It sets addEOFNL=true and breaks before the second marker can set removeEOFNL. Lines 70-72 then run `if (lines[lines.length - 1] != '') lines.push('')`. Trace: source 'line1
line2
line3
line4' gives 'line1
line2
line3
line44
' instead of '...line44'. The baseline returned 'line1
line2
line3
line44'. So applyPatch(old, createPatch(old, new)) no longer reproduces `new`.

findings.reason: If the source ends in a newline, the addEOFNL branch still returns false at fuzzFactor 0 (apply.js:73-74), and with fuzz>0 it still does nothing, the same as the baseline. That rejection is not lost. The only real change in behaviour is the no-newline case, which is the C1/X1 item.
findings.claim: Removing the both-sides-no-EOFNL validation means a source that ends in a newline is no longer rejected at fuzzFactor 0.
findings.evidence: The diff removes `if (addEOFNL) { if (!fuzzFactor && lines[lines.length - 1] == '') { return false; } }` and its comment ('we simply validate that the source file has no trailing newline'). Since the loop now breaks early, removeEOFNL and addEOFNL can no longer both be true, so this check cannot be restored as written. The addEOFNL branch at lines 70-75 is not equivalent: when the source has no trailing newline it pushes a newline instead of leaving the file alone.

findings.reason: Every marker in test/patch/apply.js (lines 133, 150, 166, 199, 326, 1417, 1505, 1519, 1535, 1549) appears once per hunk. No test applies the two-marker form, so the suite cannot catch C1. Lowered from medium to low because this is a test gap, not a bug in its own right.
findings.claim: No applyPatch test covers a final hunk with two `\ No newline at end of file` markers, so the regression passes the suite.
findings.evidence: Every `\ No newline at end of file` case in test/patch/apply.js (for example lines 133, 150, 166, 199, 326, 1417, 1505, 1519, 1549) has only one marker in the hunk. The two-marker form appears only in test/patch/create.js:93-107 and :123-139, which test createPatch output and never apply it.
